flags.name: accept-terms-of-use
flags.usage: Accepts Terms and Conditions (for non-interactive environments).

flags.name: config-file
flags.usage: Filepath to a yaml file with flag values.

flags.name: api-timeout
flags.usage: Specifies the timeout value for API requests in seconds.

flags.name: chain-config-file
flags.usage: Path to a YAML file with chain config values.

flags.name: e2e-config
flags.usage: Enables the E2E testing config, only for use within end-to-end testing.

flags.name: grpc-max-msg-size
flags.usage:
WARNING: The gRPC API will remain the default and fully supported through v8 (expected in 2026) but will be eventually removed in favor of REST API..
		Integer to define max receive message call size (in bytes).
		If serving a public gRPC server, set this to a more reasonable size to avoid
		resource exhaustion from large messages. 
		Validators with as many as 10000 keys can be run with a max message size of less than 
		50Mb. The default here is set to a very high value for local users.

flags.name: minimal-config
flags.usage: Uses minimal config with parameters as defined in the spec.

flags.name: rpc-max-page-size
flags.usage: Max number of items returned per page in RPC responses for paginated endpoints.

flags.name: tls-cert
flags.usage: Certificate for secure gRPC. Pass this and the tls-key flag in order to use gRPC securely.

flags.name: chain-id
flags.usage: Sets the chain id of the beacon chain

flags.name: disable-debug-rpc-endpoints
flags.usage: Disables the debug Beacon API namespace.

flags.name: http-cors-domain
flags.usage: Comma separated list of domains from which to accept cross origin requests.

flags.name: http-host
flags.usage: Host on which the HTTP server runs on.

flags.name: http-port
flags.usage: Port on which the HTTP server runs on.

flags.name: tls-key
flags.usage: Key for secure gRPC. Pass this and the tls-cert flag in order to use gRPC securely.

flags.name: network-id
flags.usage: Sets the network id of the beacon chain.

flags.name: rpc-host
flags.usage: Host on which the RPC server should listen

flags.name: rpc-port
flags.usage: RPC port exposed by a beacon node

flags.name: batch-verifier-limit
flags.usage: Maximum number of signatures to batch verify at once for beacon attestation p2p gossip.

flags.name: state-diff-exponents
flags.usage: A comma-separated list of exponents (of 2) in decreasing order, defining the state diff hierarchy levels. The last exponent must be greater than or equal to 5.

flags.name: archive-origin-state
flags.usage: Path to an ssz-encoded beacon state at an epoch boundary slot, used as the oldest state an archive node will hold. Defaults to the genesis state. Requires --enable-archive.

flags.name: postpone-shutdown-for-proposals
flags.usage: On a graceful shutdown signal (SIGINT/SIGTERM, e.g. Ctrl-C on Linux), postpone shutdown if a connected validator client must propose a block in the next 2 epochs. Send the signal again to force the node to stop immediately.

flags.name: disable-graffiti-client-append
flags.usage: Disables appending consensus and execution client version information to the block graffiti

flags.name: bootstrap-node
flags.usage: The enr/enode address of bootstrap node. Beacon node will connect for peer discovery via DHT. Multiple nodes can be passed by using the flag multiple times but not comma-separated. You can also pass YAML files containing multiple nodes.

flags.name: enable-upnp
flags.usage: Enable the service (Beacon chain or Validator) to use UPnP when possible.

flags.name: no-discovery
flags.usage: Enable only local network p2p and do not connect to cloud bootstrap nodes

flags.name: p2p-allowlist
flags.usage: The CIDR subnet for allowing only certain peer connections. Using "public" would allow only public subnets. Example: 192.168.0.0/16 would permit connections to peers on your local network only. The default is to accept all connections.

flags.name: p2p-denylist
flags.usage: The CIDR subnets for denying certainty peer connections. Using "private" would deny all private subnets. Example: 192.168.0.0/16 would deny connections from peers on your local network only. The default is to accept all connections.

flags.name: p2p-colocation-whitelist
flags.usage: CIDR addresses to exempt from gossip sub IP colocation restrictions. Can be specified multiple times. Example: 192.168.1.1/32 would exempt that specific IP from colocation restrictions.

flags.name: p2p-host-ip
flags.usage: The IP address advertised by libp2p. This may be used to advertise an external IP.

flags.name: p2p-host-dns
flags.usage: The DNS address advertised by libp2p. This may be used to advertise an external DNS.

flags.name: p2p-local-ip
flags.usage: The local ip address to listen for incoming data.

flags.name: p2p-max-peers
flags.usage: The max number of p2p peers to maintain.

flags.name: p2p-priv-key
flags.usage: The file containing the private key to use in communications with other peers.

flags.name: p2p-quic-port
flags.usage: The QUIC port used by libp2p.

flags.name: p2p-static-id
flags.usage: Enables the peer id of the node to be fixed by saving the generated network key to the default key path.

flags.name: p2p-tcp-port
flags.usage: The TCP port used by libp2p.

flags.name: p2p-udp-port
flags.usage: The UDP port used by the discovery service discv5.

flags.name: pubsub-queue-size
flags.usage: The size of the pubsub validation and outbound queue for the node.

flags.name: relay-node
flags.usage: The address of relay node. The beacon node will connect to the relay node and advertise their address via the relay node to other peers

flags.name: peer
flags.usage: Connect with this peer, this flag may be used multiple times. This peer is recognized as a trusted peer.Accepts enode, multiaddr, and enr formats.

flags.name: blob-batch-limit
flags.usage: The amount of blobs the local peer is bounded to request and respond to in a batch.

flags.name: blob-batch-limit-burst-factor
flags.usage: The factor by which blob batch limit may increase on burst.

flags.name: data-column-batch-limit
flags.usage: The amount of data columns the local peer is bounded to request and respond to in a batch.

flags.name: data-column-batch-limit-burst-factor
flags.usage: The factor by which data column batch limit may increase on burst.

flags.name: disable-partial-data-columns
flags.usage: Disables cell-level dissemination for PeerDAS data columns, falling back to full column gossip.

flags.name: block-batch-limit
flags.usage: The amount of blocks the local peer is bounded to request and respond to in a batch. Maximum 128

flags.name: block-batch-limit-burst-factor
flags.usage: The factor by which block batch limit may increase on burst.

flags.name: max-concurrent-dials
flags.usage: Sets the maximum number of peers that a node will attempt to dial with from discovery. By default we will dials as many peers as possible.

flags.name: minimum-peers-per-subnet
flags.usage: Sets the minimum number of peers that a node will attempt to peer with that are subscribed to a subnet.

flags.name: min-sync-peers
flags.usage: The required number of valid peers to connect with before syncing.

flags.name: subscribe-all-subnets
flags.usage: Subscribe to all possible attestation and sync subnets.

flags.name: supernode
flags.usage: Custodies all data. Cannot be used with --semi-supernode.

flags.name: semi-supernode
flags.usage: Custodies just enough data to serve the blobs and blob sidecars beacon API. Cannot be used with --supernode.

flags.name: backfill-batch-size
flags.usage: Number of blocks per backfill batch. A larger number will request more blocks at once from peers, but also consume more system memory to hold batches in memory during processing. This has a multiplicative effect with backfill-worker-count.

flags.name: backfill-worker-count
flags.usage: Number of concurrent backfill batch requests. A larger number will better utilize network resources, up to a system-dependent limit, but will also consume more system memory to hold batches in memory during processing. Multiply by backfill-batch-size and average block size (~2MB before deneb) to find the right number for your system. This has a multiplicative effect with backfill-batch-size.

flags.name: enable-backfill
flags.usage: Backfill will only be enabled when this flag is specified on a node using checkpoint sync.

flags.name: clear-db
flags.usage: Prompt for clearing any previously stored data at the data directory.

flags.name: datadir
flags.usage: Data directory for the databases.

flags.name: force-clear-db
flags.usage: Clears any previously stored data at the data directory.

flags.name: restore-source-file
flags.usage: Filepath to the backed-up database file which will be used to restore the database

flags.name: restore-target-dir
flags.usage: Target directory of the restored database

flags.name: backfill-oldest-slot
flags.usage: Specifies the oldest slot that backfill should download. If this value is greater than current_slot - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS, it will be ignored with a warning log.

flags.name: blob-retention-epochs
flags.usage: Override the default blob retention period (measured in epochs). The node will exit with an error at startup if the value is less than the default of 4096 epochs.

flags.name: beacon-db-pruning
flags.usage: Enables pruning of beacon db beyond MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS duration. This is an opt-in feature, and should only be enabled if operators doesn't require historical data.

flags.name: pruner-retention-epochs
flags.usage: Specifies the retention period for the pruner service in terms of epochs. If this value is less than MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS, it will be ignored.

flags.name: slots-per-archive-point
flags.usage: The slot durations of when an archived state gets saved in the beaconDB.

flags.name: blob-storage-layout
flags.usage: Dictates how to organize the blob directory structure on disk, available options are: flat, by-epoch.
flags.default: "by-epoch", unless a different existing layout is detected

flags.name: blob-path
flags.usage: Location for blob storage. Default location will be a 'blobs' directory next to the beacon db.

flags.name: data-column-path
flags.usage: Location for data column storage. Default location will be a 'data-columns' directory next to the beacon db.

flags.name: local-block-value-boost
flags.usage: A percentage boost for local block construction as a Uint64. This is used to prioritize local block construction over relay/builder block constructionBoost is an additional percentage to multiple local block value. Use builder block if: builder_bid_value * 100 > local_block_value * (local-block-value-boost + 100)

flags.name: max-builder-consecutive-missed-slots
flags.usage: Number of consecutive skip slot to fallback from using relay/builder to local execution engine for block construction

flags.name: max-builder-epoch-missed-slots
flags.usage: Number of total skip slot to fallback from using relay/builder to local execution engine for block construction in last epoch rolling window

flags.name: http-mev-relay
flags.usage: A MEV builder relay string http endpoint, this will be used to interact MEV builder network using API defined in: https://ethereum.github.io/builder-specs/#/Builder

flags.name: min-builder-bid
flags.usage: An absolute value in Gwei that the builder bid has to have in order for this beacon node to use the builder's block. Anything less than this value and the beacon will revert to local building.

flags.name: min-builder-to-local-difference
flags.usage: An absolute value in Gwei that the builder bid has to have in order for this beacon node to use the builder's block. Anything less than this value and the beacon will revert to local building.

flags.name: builder-header-timeout
flags.usage: Timeout to use when fetching a block header from the builder API, as a duration (e.g. 1s, 2s, 2500ms). Must be greater than 0. Only effective up to the Fulu fork.

flags.name: builder-bid-timeout
flags.usage: Timeout to use when fetching execution payload bids from the builder API, as a duration (e.g. 600ms, 1s). Must be greater than 0. Only effective from the Gloas fork onward.

flags.name: suggested-fee-recipient
flags.usage: Post bellatrix, this address will receive the transaction fees produced by any blocks from this node. Default to junk whilst bellatrix is in development state. Validator client can override this value through the preparebeaconproposer api.

flags.name: disable-builder-ssz
flags.usage: Disables SSZ encoding for Builder API requests and responses, using JSON instead.

flags.name: builder-allowed-failures
flags.usage: Number of payload delivery failures a builder is allowed before this node blacklists it.

flags.name: builder-critical-failures
flags.usage: Failure count at which a builder earns the longer blacklist set by --builder-critical-blacklist-period.

flags.name: builder-blacklist-period
flags.usage: Number of epochs a builder stays blacklisted on its first offense. Must be greater than 0.

flags.name: builder-critical-blacklist-period
flags.usage: Number of epochs a builder stays blacklisted once it reaches --builder-critical-failures.

flags.name: builder-relay-blacklist-period
flags.usage: Maximum number of epochs a direct connection endpoint stays banned for serving a builder that failed to reveal a payload. Never exceeds the offending builder's own blacklist.

flags.name: builder-failure-backoff-period
flags.usage: Number of epochs without a failure after which a builder's failure counter resets to zero.

flags.name: builder-critical-failed-builders
flags.usage: Number of concurrently blacklisted builders that forces this node to fall back to self-building. Must be greater than 0.

flags.name: checkpoint-block
flags.usage: Rather than syncing from genesis, you can start processing from a ssz-serialized BeaconState+Block. This flag allows you to specify a local file containing the checkpoint Block to load.

flags.name: checkpoint-sync-url
flags.usage: URL of a synced beacon node to trust in obtaining checkpoint sync data. As an additional safety measure, it is strongly recommended to only use this option in conjunction with --weak-subjectivity-checkpoint flag

flags.name: checkpoint-state
flags.usage: Rather than syncing from genesis, you can start processing from a ssz-serialized BeaconState+Block. This flag allows you to specify a local file containing the checkpoint BeaconState to load.

flags.name: weak-subjectivity-checkpoint
flags.usage: Input in `block_root:epoch_number` format. This guarantees that syncing leads to the given Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint along the canonical chain. If such a sync is not possible, the node will treat it as a critical and irrecoverable failure

flags.name: genesis-beacon-api-url
flags.usage: URL of a synced beacon node to trust for obtaining genesis state. As an additional safety measure, it is strongly recommended to only use this option in conjunction with --weak-subjectivity-checkpoint flag

flags.name: genesis-state
flags.usage: Load a genesis state from ssz file. Testnet genesis files can be found in the eth2-clients/eth2-testnets repository on github.

flags.name: contract-deployment-block
flags.usage: The eth1 block in which the deposit contract was deployed.

flags.name: deposit-contract
flags.usage: Deposit contract address. Beacon chain node will listen logs coming from the deposit contract to determine when validator is eligible to participate.

flags.name: engine-endpoint-timeout-seconds
flags.usage: Sets the execution engine timeout (seconds) for execution payload semantics (forkchoiceUpdated, newPayload)

flags.name: eth1-header-req-limit
flags.usage: Sets the maximum number of headers that a deposit log query can fetch.

flags.name: execution-endpoint
flags.usage: An execution client http endpoint. Can contain auth header as well in the format

flags.name: execution-headers
flags.usage: A comma separated list of key value pairs to pass as HTTP headers for all execution client calls. Example: --execution-headers=key1=value1,key2=value2

flags.name: jwt-secret
flags.usage: REQUIRED if connecting to an execution node via HTTP. Provides a path to a file containing a hex-encoded string representing a 32 byte secret used for authentication with an execution node via HTTP. If this is not set, all requests to execution nodes via HTTP for consensus-related calls will fail, which will prevent your validators from performing their duties. This is not required if using an IPC connection.

flags.name: jwt-id
flags.usage: JWT claims id. Could be used to identify the client

flags.name: disable-monitoring
flags.usage: Disables monitoring service.

flags.name: enable-tracing
flags.usage: Enables OpenTelemetry tracing.

flags.name: monitoring-host
flags.usage: Host used for listening and responding metrics for prometheus.

flags.name: trace-sample-fraction
flags.usage: Head-sampling ratio applied to every trace started by the process. 1.0 keeps all traces.

flags.name: tracing-endpoint
flags.usage: OTLP/HTTP endpoint that traces are exported to (e.g. an OpenTelemetry Collector or a Tempo receiver).

flags.name: tracing-process-name
flags.usage: Name to apply to tracing tag `process_name`.

flags.name: monitor-indices
flags.usage: List of validator indices to track performance

flags.name: monitoring-port
flags.usage: Port used to listening and respond metrics for Prometheus.

flags.name: historical-slasher-node
flags.usage: Enables required flags for serving historical data to a slasher client. Results in additional storage usage

flags.name: slasher-datadir
flags.usage: Directory for the slasher database

flags.name: slasher
flags.usage: Enables a slasher in the beacon node for detecting slashable offenses.

flags.name: disable-log-colors
flags.usage: Disable color formatting for terminal logs.

flags.name: log-format
flags.usage: Specifies log formatting. Supports: text, json, fluentd, journald.

flags.name: log-file
flags.usage: Specifies log file name, relative or absolute.

flags.name: verbosity
flags.usage: Logging verbosity. (trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, panic)

flags.name: disable-ephemeral-log-file
flags.usage: Disables the creation of a debug log file that keeps 24 hours of logs.

flags.name: log.vmodule
flags.usage: Per-package log verbosity. packagePath=level entries separated by commas.

flags.name: save-invalid-block-temp
flags.usage: Writes invalid blocks to temp directory.

flags.name: save-invalid-blob-temp
flags.usage: Writes invalid blobs to temp directory.

flags.name: disable-grpc-connection-logging
flags.usage:
WARNING: The gRPC API will remain the default and fully supported through v8 (expected in 2026) but will be eventually removed in favor of REST API..
		Disables displaying logs for newly connected grpc clients.

flags.name: sepolia
flags.usage: Runs Prysm configured for the Sepolia test network.

flags.name: hoodi
flags.usage: Runs Prysm configured for the Hoodi test network.

flags.name: mainnet
flags.usage: Runs on Ethereum main network. This is the default and can be omitted.

flags.name: disable-peer-scorer
flags.usage: (Danger): Disables P2P peer scorer. Do NOT use this in production!

flags.name: disable-broadcast-slashings
flags.usage: Disables broadcasting slashings submitted to the beacon node.

flags.name: disable-staking-contract-check
flags.usage: Disables checking of staking contract deposits when proposing blocks, useful for devnets.

flags.name: save-full-execution-payloads
flags.usage: Saves beacon blocks with full execution payloads instead of execution payload headers in the database.

flags.name: ignore-unviable-attestations
flags.usage: Ignores attestations whose target state is not viable with respect to the current head (avoid expensive state replay from lagging attesters).

flags.name: disable-track-equivocations
flags.usage: Disables recording proposer equivocations observed on gossip into forkchoice.

flags.name: enable-full-ssz-data-logging
flags.usage: Enables displaying logs for full ssz data on rejected gossip messages.

flags.name: disable-verbose-sig-verification
flags.usage: Disables identifying invalid signatures if batch verification fails when processing block.

flags.name: enable-proposer-preprocessing
flags.usage: Enables proposer pre-processing of blocks before proposing.

flags.name: prepare-all-payloads
flags.usage: Informs the engine to prepare all local payloads. Useful for relayers and builders.

flags.name: disable-resource-manager
flags.usage: Disables running the libp2p resource manager.

flags.name: enable-light-client
flags.usage: Enables the light client support in the beacon node

flags.name: blob-save-fsync
flags.usage: Forces new blob files to be fysnc'd before continuing, ensuring durable blob writes.

flags.name: disable-quic
flags.usage: Disables connecting using the QUIC protocol with peers.

flags.name: enable-discovery-reboot
flags.usage: Experimental: Enables the discovery listener to rebooted in the event of connectivity issues.

flags.name: enable-experimental-attestation-pool
flags.usage: Enables an experimental attestation pool design.

flags.name: enable-fast-confirmation
flags.usage: Enables the fast confirmation rule (FCR) for rapid block confirmation under synchrony assumptions.

flags.name: enable-state-diff
flags.usage: Enables the state diff feature.

flags.name: enable-archive
flags.usage:
Turns the node into an archive node: backfills blocks down to the archive origin state (see --archive-origin-state, genesis by default)
		and then regenerates every historical state into the state-diff tree. (Implies --enable-state-diff and --enable-backfill.)

flags.name: sync-from
flags.usage: Forces the head of the beacon chain to a specific block root. Values can be 'head' or a block root. The block root has to be known to the beacon node and correspond to a block newer than the current finalized checkpoint.

flags.name: blacklist-roots
flags.usage: A comma-separatted list of 0x-prefixed hexstrings. Declares blocks with the given blockroots to be invalid. It downscores peers that send these blocks.

flags.name: enable-hashtree
flags.usage: (Experimental): Enables the hashtree hashing library.

flags.name: disable-builder-relay-circuit-breaker
flags.usage: Stops the builder circuit breaker from tracking which builders each direct connection endpoint serves, so a failing builder no longer bans the endpoints serving it.

flags.name: disable-last-epoch-targets
flags.usage: Deprecated: disables processing of last epoch targets.

flags.name: enable-historical-state-representation
flags.usage: Enables the beacon chain to save historical states in a space efficient manner. (Warning): Once enabled, this feature migrates your database in to a new schema and there is no going back. At worst, your entire database might get corrupted.

flags.name: dev
flags.usage: Enables experimental features still in development. These features may not be stable.

flags.name: holesky
flags.usage: Runs Prysm configured for the Holesky test network.

flags.name: terminal-total-difficulty-override
flags.usage: Sets the total difficulty to manual overrides the default TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY value. WARNING: This flag should be used only if you have a clear understanding that community has decided to override the terminal difficulty. Incorrect usage will result in your node experience consensus failure.

flags.name: terminal-block-hash-override
flags.usage: Sets the block hash to manual overrides the default TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH value. WARNING: This flag should be used only if you have a clear understanding that community has decided to override the terminal block hash. Incorrect usage will result in your node experience consensus failure.

flags.name: terminal-block-hash-epoch-override
flags.usage: Sets the block hash epoch to manual overrides the default TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH_ACTIVATION_EPOCH value. WARNING: This flag should be used only if you have a clear understanding that community has decided to override the terminal block hash activation epoch. Incorrect usage will result in your node experience consensus failure.

flags.name: subscribe-all-data-subnets
flags.usage: Deprecated alias of --supernode.

flags.name: enable-experimental-backfill
flags.usage: Deprecated alias of --enable-backfill.

flags.name: extend-blob-retention-epoch
flags.usage: Deprecated alias of --blob-retention-epochs.

flags.name: max-goroutines
flags.usage: Deprecated alias of --healthz-max-goroutines.

flags.name: healthz-max-goroutines
flags.usage: The /healthz endpoint reports the node as unhealthy if the average goroutine count during a 10 slots window exceeds this threshold.

flags.name: blockprofilerate
flags.usage: Turns on block profiling with the given rate.

flags.name: memprofilerate
flags.usage: Turns on memory profiling with the given rate.

flags.name: mutexprofilefraction
flags.usage: Turns on mutex profiling with the given rate.

flags.name: pprofaddr
flags.usage: pprof HTTP server listening interface.

flags.name: pprof
flags.usage: Enables the pprof HTTP server.

flags.name: pprofport
flags.usage: pprof HTTP server listening port.

flags.name: gc-percent
flags.usage: The percentage of freshly allocated data to live data on which the gc will be run again.

commands.name: db
commands.usage: Defines commands for interacting with the Ethereum Beacon Node database

subcommands.name: restore
subcommands.description: restores a database from a backup file

flags.name: restore-source-file
flags.usage: Filepath to the backed-up database file which will be used to restore the database

flags.name: restore-target-dir
flags.usage: Target directory of the restored database

commands.name: generate-auth-secret
commands.usage: creates a random, 32 byte hex string in a plaintext file to be used for authenticating JSON-RPC requests. If no --output-file flag is defined, the file will be created in the current working directory
commands.description: creates a random, 32 byte hex string in a plaintext file to be used for authenticating JSON-RPC requests. If no --output-file flag is defined, the file will be created in the current working directory

flags.name: output-file
flags.usage: Target file path for outputting a generated JWT secret to be used for JSON-RPC authentication
